title: UX research plan: how to write one (with examples)
summary: Learn to write a UX research plan that ties objectives, questions, and methods to one decision, with worked examples and a step-by-step framework.
body_markdown:
How do I write a UX research plan that starts with the product decision instead of the research method? +


Start the UX research plan with the decision question, then let it set the method, sample size, participant criteria, interview guide, and analysis plan. Choosing the method first leaves the research study without a decision to prove. A discussion guide built without that decision collects anecdotes a product team cannot act on.


What should a UX research plan include to connect business goals, research objectives, and interview questions? +


A UX research plan connects business objectives to research objectives through one decision question. It specifies the discussion guide, coding categories, comparison logic, and required evidence.


How can I tell whether a research question will produce evidence a product team can actually act on? +


A research question is actionable when it maps to a named decision and yields patterns across research participants rather than anecdotes. Otherwise, revise the research plan.


How can AI help with a UX research plan? +


AI helps most with fieldwork and analysis. An AI research assistant can run AI-moderated interviews, ask follow-up questions when an answer is vague, and extract the researcher's coding categories across every interview. The researcher still writes the decision question and decides what the evidence means.


Are there UX research plan templates that trace each interview question back to an objective and product decision? +


Yes, but templates work only when each of your \[user interview questions\](/insights/user-interview-questions) is tagged to a decision question and analysis plan. A research plan helps most as a one-page cheat sheet of six steps: decision question, method, behavioral screener, interview guide, analysis plan, and output requirements, with every field mapped to the decision.
